[LIMP.12.2] **The built-in schemas.** Each is defined by the clause the table
names, and the compiler must declare it exactly as that clause states: its
name, its scope and lifetime, and its slots in the clause's order. A schema is
written into an artefact when the program uses it: when the condition its row
gives holds, or when the program names the schema. A built-in schema the
program does not use is left out.

| Schema | Defined by | Written into the artefact |
|---|---|---|
| `ComputationError` | [LERR.9.2] | always ([LERR.9.4]) |
| `TypeError` | [LERR.9.3] | always ([LERR.9.4]) |
| `CallError` | [LCRS.4.2.1] | when the program contains a `call` action |
| `HydrationComplete` | [LHYD.5.1] | when the program dispatches a hydration call ([LHYD.6.3.1]) |
| `HydratedSample` | [LHYD.4.3.1] | when the program dispatches a `hydrate_samples` call |
| `TimeZoneOffset` | [LTIM.10.6] | always |

`CallError` is written for every program with a `call`, whether or not a rule
matches it, because an adapter may assert one for any call ([LCRS.4.2.2],
[LCRS.17.1]). `TimeZoneOffset` is written for every program, because the
integrator supplies its facts whatever the program reads ([LTIM.10.10]).

A rule that matches `CallError` in a program with no `call` is inert, since no
adapter answers a call the program never makes. Its schema is still written,
because the rule names it, and an artefact whose `AlphaNode` names a schema it
lacks is refused at load ([RDSC.8.7]).
